instruments.title: Water drum. Slightly waisted tubular drum with solid figure carved on front that has flat face rear. Penis intact, its tip covered with green gloss paint. Eye inlay lost and sockets painted with green gloss. Rougher face design than 1935.23B. At back lug formed by pierced neck extension which is near base of head. Two thicknesses of rough cane tied through this lug.

Sacred bamboo flute covered for most of its length, except mouth-hole, with plaited cane sleeves, coloured blackish red. Black cassowary feathers attached round coiled cane work flange at base and at approximately mid-length. Flute ornament in shape of a pig's head with fish's body and tail projecting above end of bamboo.

Sacred bamboo flute covered for most of its length, except for mouth-hole, with plaited cane sleeves, coloured blackish red. Black cassowary feathers attached to the coiled cane work flange at mid-length.

household.title: Bamboo hoe with curved digging end. Cut from a length of bamboo. The curved end has been cut to form a point. [AB [OPS Move] 5/1/2017]

Bilum, almost square bag netted from thick twine in double figure of 8 rows. Natural and reddish brown loop stitching attaches separately netted rim band. Netted carrying strap crosses over from top corners. Design in contrasting blue and reddish brown dyed twine against natural pale brown colour. At top a complex zigzag of striped trapezoids with chequered parallelograms, partly linked across top by border band of brown, and joined across bottom by series of blue, brown and blue narrow bands. In centre a thick brown stripe with ribbed top, then four narrow ribbed bands, brown, blue, brown, blue. Below a large complex zigzag with large parallelograms spacing out the trapezoids. Made by Tshuosh, in neighbourhood of Berui village. Some stains. Original accession notes: " Pattern worked in dyed string. Carried suspended from the head by women. Bought from Tshuosh by Iatmul." Fair.

Small, almost square bilum bag, netted from thick twine in double figure of 8 rows. Dark brown coloured loop stitching attaches separately netted rim band. Netted carrying strap crosses over from top corners. 8 rows of pale blue, brown and dark brown rectangles contrast with natural/pale brown background. A few brown rectangles occur between the other rows, but the overall appearance is of a rough check design. Made by Tshuosh, in neighbourhood of Berui village. Original accession notes: " Pattern worked in dyed string. Carried suspended from the head by women. Bought from Tshuosh by Iatmul." Good.

Bilum bag netted from thick twine in double figure of 8 rows. Reddish brown loop stitching attaches separately netted rim band. Netted carrying strap crosses over from top corners. Design of contrasting blue and reddish brown dyed twine netted in against natural pale brown colour. Three broad horizontal bands each composed of paired blue and reddish brown narrow bands, and with natural bands left between each broad band. Each with a slightly darker brown stripe through their centres. Made by Tshuosh, in neighbourhood of Berui village. Original accession notes: " Pattern worked in dyed string. Carried suspended from the head by women. Bought from Tshuosh by Iatmul." Good.

Bag netted from thick twine in double figure of 8 rows. Design in contrasting reddish brown and dull blue netted in against natural pale brown colour. Made by Tshuosh, in neighbourhood of Berui village. Carried suspended from the head by women.

Full-length male hook figure on 2-pronged hook base. Ovoid head with fine black on white face painting. Conus shell eye inlay. Initiatory marks on breasts and navel are represented in white paint which also decorated the tip of the penis and the knees.

Human head on tiered trunk with a bird each side of trunk centre, and 2-pronged hook base. Elaborate facial paint on head, cowrie shell eye inlay, grooved forehead. With fibre tassels. Attributed by Iatmul to Tshambuli.

A woman's one-piece wooden paddle that has been shortened, the shaft end now a rough point. Narrow lanceolate blade which is carved on its lower half, either side of a mid-rib, with ovoid ' eyes' and plain and toothed crescent curves. Shaft top carved with design of zigzag infilled ovoids between curved verticals, and a zigzag band underneath.

A man's paddle that may have been cut down to create a woman's paddle. Carved design on one face of the lanceolate blade with 5 faces and several ' eyes', with plain, toothed curves, zigzags, and bar.. Slightly raised shaft top with two projecting ovals at the sides, that are incised with a knob and bar design, inside a ring border. The whole appears to be encrusted with a thin layer of mud or brown paint.

Carved fowl's head, broken off at neck, touches of red and white paint on crest. Narrow raised beak and cheek to eye design. Slight piercing of cheek pouches. Figure broken. Original accession notes: " Carving of a domestic fowl, ? part of a lime pot." Fair
Pair of false breasts made of conical gourd halves worn by men on ceremonial occasions. eg. Naven and in certain initiatory ceremonies, in which the initiators are spoken of as NYAME ("Mothers")

Representation - Narrow openwork wooden board, carved with distinct face and 4 hook prongs in each of 2 windows near base. Toothed top with central boss, a point with raised oval ' eyes' . Ovoid face set in side curves with hook eyes and long nose ridge pierced with 4 strutted tear shapes. Nose-ridge continues down to ' chest' area. Spiral or hook curve cheek marks circule out from the nose. Mouth also has side curves. Main body panel has two bird's heads with vertically interlocking beaks in centre. Two other bird's beaks point straight out from nose ridge near top of body panel. Rest of panel filled with pierced ' lobefaces' . Base carved with spirals or hook curves, corners rounded and small butt in centre of bottom edge. No face at rear. Traces of red, black & white paint, thickest on face, especially the white background. Rough overcoiled cane loop attached through piercings in top of nose ridge. Cracked with pieces missing, colours faded. Original accession notes: " Large openwork carving representing the face of the sago-beetle (PANANGUN). These objects are said to be no longer made (? ceased to be made before white contact). They are kept in dwelling houses but I do not know their significance. From the arrangement of the bottom of the plank I judge they are a type of ceremonial hook probably " altars" of some kind. No other specimens were seen in the houses." Poor

Narrow openwork wooden board carved with distinct face and 2 curved hook prongs in each of 2 windows near base. Toothed top with piereced point as central boss and pierced semioval ' ears' at corners. Rough overcoiled loop attached through piercings. Slight curve design on the forehead. Hook eyes. Long nose with pierced bird design in profile with a knobbed beak ridge. Nose reaches to ' chest' . Cheek marks semiovoid, lying at base of cheek area. Crescent mouth with two globular curls at each side, followed by triangular tips. Main body panel carved with 2 bird's in centre whose beaks interlock round rod. Pierced lobefaces cover rest of body panel. Base carved with scroll or spiral design. Baseline flat except for rounded corners and point projecting in centre. Faint remains of white (particularly on face background and on the uppermost birds), red and black pigments. No face at rear. An old crack lies across lower half, now glued. Rough cane bindings which formerly held pieces together still in place. Colours faded. Original accession notes: " Large openwork carving representing the face of the sago-beetle (cf. 1930.341)." Fair

Almost triangular openwork wooden board carved with distinct face at top and 4 hook prongs, 2 each side of central bar, near base. Capped headtop above central piercing, and oval painted in middle of forehead. Concentric oval ring eyes, club nose with crescentic nostrils or base, oval mouth. Chevron cheek marks, connected with eye (?). Main body panel carved with single pair of birds with vertically interlocking tails in centre. Additional birds at each corner, top birds lie right up next to face. Between corner birds along sides are lobefaces.

Lime gourd. Broad curved gourd, with oval cross-section. Upper half incised with design of 2 large faces with smaller faces inset in the nose area. Infilled with charcoal. Two other faces upside down between the large faces at bottom. Plain fringe at base. At top oval rings in wavy lines and scalloped border. Said to have been manufactured by Tshambuli. Original accession notes: " Ornamented with faces which the Iatmul describe as WINDSHIMBU - spirits which live in trees and occasionally act as shamanic spirits possessing men and are impersonated by the initiates when water-drums are shown to novices. WINDSHIMBU are also identified with flutes, which are in myth said to be derived from the cut-off penis of WINDSHIMBU. This type of ornamentation of lime-gourds is practised among the Iatmul and (?) in Tshambuli. I do not know where it originated. The word WINDSHIMBU is probably etymologically connected with UNDUMBU (= ghosts). But at the present time these two types of spiritual being are clearly discriminated." Good
Lime box. Bamboo tube with wooden ornament in shape of a janus-face at top of barred ovoid, with a bird on a 'nose' at the ovoid's tip. Decorated with blue. white and red paint and many tassels.
Beater for gong. Stick with rounded base and flattened pointed tip with toothed section and two small round lugs above the narrower handle section. No colouring or surface carving.
Beater for gong. Stick with circular cross-section and small conical stepped butt. Tip expanded and rounded with face carved on one side. No colouring, carving very shallow.

Beater for gong. Stick with expanded base, cylindrical handle and carved tapering point, with janus heads at bottom. Tip broken off. Lugs at right angles to faces rather than same sides as in 1930.576. Separated by tiny triangular knobs. Heads have oval raised eyes (one head with ring carved inside the ovals), delicate club noses and raised crescent mouths.

sculpture.title: Elément de maquette de maison cérémonielle
Sculpture de faîtage de maison cérémonielle

A Nggwail representation which may represent a shamanic spirit, Lamwail. A full-length wooden figure with large ovoid head fringed with human hair, border covered in red gum studded with nassa and cowrie shells, and along forehead conus shells.

Small full-length wooden female figure used for love magic. With a large head and sharply bent elbows and knees. Hands rest either side of back of head and feet at each end of a bar at the base. Tongue visible in oval mouth. Tassels in nose, wrists, waist, neck and one ankle and oval eyes with nassa shell inlay. Very prominent genitals and possible anus at rear.

Long narrow full-length figure with bird on its back carved in a pale hard wood. Has two loop slots to take pole in front. Traces of black paint on man's face and arms. Feet, ankles and base painted black, with some red paint on the side of the right leg and the front side of the bottom loop slot. Rough carving, with chisel marks still visible. Head ovoid with raised cap, oval ring and dot eyes, raised crescent mouth, pierced club nose with twist of palm knotted through it. Narrow double pierced ears, very long neck. Arms hang to the sides of the elongated trunk and are joined to it at the elbow by the second loop slat. Hands rest above the thighs with fingers carved, but of a rough round outline. Hollow belly with loop slat across it. Male genitals prominent. Legs bent slightly at the knees where the other loop slat is, and the stump feet rest on the top of the triangular pointed base which has a large central groove. Bird has lug in wattle or pouch position on underside of neck. 8 lugs down bird's back, and toothed curve design incised lightly on bird's folded wings with a face at the top of each wing. Below the bird's tail is a second bracket reaching to the bottom of the man's trunk. Bird's legs bent with talons carved. Feet rest on back of man's head. Bird has knob eyes, knob ears and a plain curved beak. Fibre ear and nose rings for human figure. Original accession notes: " A recent carving, bored to fix on a pole, representing a man NDO and a WAWI (a species of bird). This specimen was not regarded seriously, but ' it would have had to be hidden if it had been old' ." Fair

garment.title: échantillons de fibres pour fabriquer une jupe
Lens-shaped wooden head with face carved both sides, small pierced cap with fibre and reed string through piercing. Made of pale light wood, stained a darker black/brown.

Lens-shaped light wood head with red/brown paint overall and rounded back. Small rounded head cap, sharply raised slant eyes. Bulbous nose with narrow flanges for nostrils. Down-curved mouth. Laterally pierced ' bearded' chin. No ears.

Ovoid wooden head with small cap top, curved back. Yellow with a little red colouring. Thick-lipped oval mouth. Narrow slanting eyes, joined to cap. Pierced delicate club shape nose. Chin extension, unpierced arch to chin tip.

jewelry.title: Ornament - Roughly ovoid shell cusp with natural striations on outside and smooth polished inside. Irregular lip ridge at top. Pierced by two small circular holes on one long side, through which a rough knotted length of twine is fastened. Twine broken, outer surface badly stained. Original accession notes: " Ornament for breast or head made of portion of melon shell and worn by either sex. For use of this ornament see Handbook, Photographs -. In these photographs a dish of European origin has been substituted for WOKTAI. Masks nos. 1935.54 and 1935.167 are decorated with representations of WOKTAI in basketwork and wood respectively." Poor

Ovoid pith head attached to centre of buttock ornament 1935.8. A few coils of hair remain on top of head and many empty holes for more coils. Face painted with fine black lines against dark yellow background.

Kait Nambu. Ovoid pith head attached to centre of buttock ornament 1935.9. Raised forehead cap, painted black. Oval eye cavities in black hook eyes. Double pierced semiovoid ear lugs with slight remains of fibre in one piercing. Squashed club nose, broad curved lips. Raised cheeks. Rear of head domed at top, with lipped cavity for lower half. Face painted with black curvilinear design against white. Badly chipped with pieces missing, paint worn.

Flat-backed wooden head with pierced ears and oval ring & dot eyes. Nose edge sharper than 1930.264A, top of head rounder, mouth more deeply incised. Tassel knots through pierced ears, small knot through nose. Same light brown coloured dark wood as 1930.264A. Plaited cord connecting the two heads used to go through top of heads, now broken.
Lens-shaped wooden head with raised eyebrow curves, oval ring and dot eyes, flattened club nose. Covered in red pigment. Attached to 1930.278 with native string.
Lens-shaped wooden head. Raised oval ring and dot eyes, club nose extending in arch to chin. Attached to 1930.277 with native fibre.

Necklace made from plaited string work in form of face with long tail at chin, bulbous forehead, loops for ears at sides, and short angled tails below the ears. Cowrie shells under forehead for eyes. Ribbed nose-loop with 2 irridescent shell hook spirals and single curved boar's tusk sliver through loop as nose ornament. Face attached to overcoiled fastening strings, one of which has large knot near its ends the other an overcoiled loop. Fibre binding ties nose ornaments together, pith padding strip holds them in place in nose loop. String work blackened on face, except for chin tail.

Necklace of plaited string work in form of face with 5 short triangular tails giving face star shape outline. Bulbous forehead, cowrie shells for eyes. Ribbed nose-loop with 2 pairs of conus shell hooks bound with string and bast fibre, for nose ornament. Reverse of face has loop in centre and 3 string, feather and red cloth strip tassels attached to loop. Broad neck band ornamented with cowrie and nassa shells at intervals. Some remains of black and red pigment. Neck band fastens by loop on one end and large knot on the other.

Necklace of plaited string work in form of face with 5 medium length tails on lower edges, 2 ear loops and stub in centre of top edge. Bulbous forehead with cowrie shell eyes below. Ribbed nose loop with no ornaments. Rear of face has loop in centre with 4 rough lengths twined string attached. Broad neck band which fastens by loop on one end and large knot on the other. Whole covered with black and faint remains of red pigment.

Necklace of plaited string work in form of face with 5 short triangular tails giving face star shape outline. Flat forehead, cowrie shells for eyes. Ribbed nose-loop with no ornaments. Rear of face has loop in centre and 1 free end of twine used to attach cowries. Broad neck band, mended in one place, fastens by loop on one end and large knot on the other. Whole covered with black and faint remains of red pigment. Neckband mended.

Dance waist ornament used by by Mwai and impersonators of Wagan. A curved rod frame is used to suspend ornaments and at present this includes the enemy portrait head (1935.10A) and long pith toggles on the spiked halo frame.

arms.title: Bow-legged wooden figure, painted on its front only. Round face with triangular nose, rough pit eyes and raised crescent lips, tiny pierced semioval ear lugs. Black knob nipples and white knob knee cap. Painted mainly red with touches of black and white. White raised pubic area with vulva slit painted in red, narrow belly with white ring round black navel. White crescent pendant/necklace, and white curves from nipples across chest. Black cap on head, black surround to eyes and as a median line on the nose. Red raised mouth with red and white stripes across the remainder of the face. Raised triangular lug on the back of the head with a fibre strand looped through it for hanging up. In this box is a fibre belt (?) probably broken off one of the figures (1935.146 or 1935.147). Original accession notes: " Wooden female figure, coloured red and marked with white patterns. There is a lug behind the head for suspension. It was probably carved for amusement, but is possibly totemic - the one theory does not exclude the other. Totemism is not always a very serious matter." Good

Arrow with three blackened, curved wooden points bound together near base with cane. All three have small, widely spaced alternate side barbs. No foreshaft. Shaft binding of diagonally crossed cane over coiled bast fibre. Tapering bamboo shaft stained red.

Arrow with three blackened wooden points bound together near base with cane. One point has only widely spaced, small alternate side barbs, other two have additional nicks along the ridges between the side barbs. No foreshaft. Shaft binding of diagonally crossed fine cane or other fibre? Tapering bamboo shaft with remains of red stain.

Arrow with two blackened wood points, bound at their base with cane. One point has prominent alternate side barbs, widely spaced; the other has small equal and opposite side barbs. No foreshaft. Shaft binding of coiled and diagonally crossed cane. Tapering bamboo shaft.

Arrow with bamboo point with nicked sides at base, rounded foreshaft tip showing. Point binding of twisted cord, 3 diagonal crossings over plain coiling. Wooden foreshaft, uncoloured, waisted in 3 places. 3 rings project at each of the upper 2 waists, 2 & 2 rings incised on upper expansion. Shaft binding of diagonally crossed cane strings, stained red. Tapering bamboo shaft with remains of red stain.

Arrow with bamboo point with nicked sides at base, pointed incised foreshaft tip showing. Point binding of fine twisted cord, 2 diagonal crossings over plain coiling. Blackened wood foreshaft, waisted in 2 places, 1 ring projects at upper waisting, 3 rings at next. 2 & 2 rings incised on upper expansion. Shaft binding of diagonally crossed cane strips, stained red. Tapering bamboo shaft, stained red.

Arrow with wooden point with small widely spaced alternate side barbs. No foreshaft. Shaft binding of roughly coiled very fine cane or tough fibre (?). Tapering bamboo shaft with remains of red stain.

ceramic.title: Pam au. A rounded necked sago earthenware jar. Applique face on one side of neck only. Pointed slightly hooked nose, double oval ring eyes and oval ring chain below similar double oval ring mouth. Plan fibre tassels through double pierced ear arcs in line with beak.

Na’u Nangk-Au. Rounded necked red earthenware jar for sago with applique face on one side of neck representing the mythical woman Demwo-Kwo-Nembit who visited Aibom in her canoe bringing dancers. Mended but still very fragile.

Paint-tray. Flat bottomed shallow ovoid bowl with rat head at one end and rough ovoid pierced tail at the other. Red paint on outside in incisions of geometrical design of ovals and curves, faint red paint on base. Original accession notes: " Animal head handle, represents MGMUT PE (rat)." Good

other.title: Flattish profile fret carving, with relief design of one main human face, and four others, two of which are double faces. Nassa shell inlay in the eyes of the main face, which has a pierced nose and pierced ears with tassel through them and through the chin.
Four sago-beetle heads are carved in profile round a lozenge shaped piece of wood which has a narrow double-rimmed hole piercing its centre vertically.

Representation - Long and narrow curved bar with raised pierced mid-rib and pig's head at either end. Mid-rib piercings are mostly oval in shape with triangular tongues left in their centres. Many red fibre tassels are tied through them. Either side of mid-rib bar are incised lines and nicks and some projecting ovals and curves which have core rings and look like ' eyes' . Painted red inside incisions, occasional black outlines, mainly white background. Under surface painted black, with remains of white and red. Series of holes pierce through from underside on one side of mid-rib only. Pig's heads have prominent tusks and elongated snouts, with rough eye rings or eye cavities and horizontal slit mouths. Painted with red and black lines against white background. Wrapped in brown paper and tied to bar is a long coil of white feathers bound with bast fibre which must have ornamented the board at one stage. Mid-rib broken and part missing, bar mended with glue, fibre tassels fraying, paint worn. Said to be loot from Tshambuli. Original accession notes: " A long carved board with longitudinal ridge. At each end is a carved representation of a pig's head. The Iatmul knew nothing of the uses of this object. In the American Natural History Museum there are comparable objects collected by Dr. Fortune from Tshuosh in the Turu area." Poor

Pair of false breasts worn by men of fine twined cane work cones with tubular apexes, one apex broken off, the other extending to a slightly expanded nozzle. Coated with thick black pigment. Paint peeling off, rims frayed.
Head made of pith-like wood. It has human hair stuck in the forehead and is decorated with white paint and black lines

Flat-backed ovoid head with strongly pointed protruding forehead. Hole pierces top of head. No ears. Narrow raised slanting eyes, raised ovoid mouth. Light wood with black/brown colouring overall. Rounded chin, tassel loop through pierced nostrils.
Large turbo shell whorl with iridescent inside and outer surface painted with design of wavy red lines alternating with white. Semi-circular wickerwork pouch, with edges sewn together, attached.

Double thick overcoiled curved cane rod with scalloped wicker frame on underside of curve and rectangular bark covered plate in centre. Long red overcoiled tail issues from tapered base of plate, pair of twisted fibre tassels are also attached. Halo of curved spikes round edge of plate framing enemy portrait head 1935.10C. 9 halo spikes have conical pith ornaments, painted red, attached. Bark piece red with white curves painted on it. Prongs broken, paint worn. Original accession notes: " Dance ornament worn suspended from waist and ornamenting buttocks. cf. 1935.8, 1935.10A/C." Poor
